text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS @

- The cabinet expressed readiness to seek a settlement of the ongoing dispute with farmers. In other decisions, the cabinet passed a resolution on reopening the Hungarian consulate in Cluj, Romania and resolved to carry out the privatisation of Raba in two phases.

- The chief organiser of farmers' demonstrations said Thursday that farmers will take to the streets in all Hungarian counties Monday to press home their demands, adding that farmers continue to insist on restoration of the tax and social insurance regulations valid last year. @
- Pig breeders suffered losses of 8 to 9 billion forints last year, claimed Matyas Balazs of the National Association of Agricultural Producers.
- A new tariff of gas and electricity prices will be introduced in June, shortly before the next energy price hike effective from July 1.
- Philips Hungary is set to build a new car radio factory in the industrial park at Gyor at a cost of $30 million, Philips President and CEO Willem van der Vegt announced yesterday. @
- After a three-day standstill due to a strike of Spanish truck drivers, the Opel factory in Szentgotthard will continue production on Monday.
- The country's largest ever issue of corporate bonds by the mobile phone company Pannon GSM closed successfully yesterday.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- A draft decree allowing the tapping of mobile phones may be submitted to the government within weeks. @

- The road border station at Udvar, the only crossing place between Serb-controlled Baranja in Croatia - still under temporary UN administration - and Hungary will be opened to international traffic on Monday.
- A total of 17 countries, including Hungary, have sent participants to a ten-day crisis management exercise held by NATO ever second year.
- The 38,000 sq m area behind Budapest's Western railway station is set to be bought and developed by Euroinvest, a company belonging to Granit Polus Rt. @
- The Slovak iron works VS Kosice is considering buying the Hungarian steel works in Ozd and the machine manufacturer Diosgyori Gepgyar.
NEPSZABADSAG

- President Arpad Goncz cabled a telegram of condolence to Chinese President Jian Zemin, Prime Minister Gyula Horn to Chinese Premier Li Peng following news of the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs Thursday received EU High Commissioner Max van der Stoel. @
- Industry and Trade Minister Szabolcs Fazakas and General Electric President and CEO Stu Fischer will sign a contract worth $200 million today, GE announced yesterday.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The Dutch firm Nationale Nerderlanden took the lead on the Hungarian life insurance market in 1996.
- The agricultural machinery producer Mezogep will sell new shares worth $20-30 million at face value to selected foreign and Hungarian institutional investors. @

- The share price of the trading company Csopak Rt skyrocketed on the stock exchange by a rarely seen 50 percent, from 2,005 forints to 3,000 forints. Trading in the shares had to be interrupted twice.
-- Budapest newsroom (36 1) 327 4040
